tasks.short: Select and fit drill bits and rods

steps.what: Consult the drill's operating and compatibility information and current hole requirements for the available bits and rods.
Select the appropriate drill bits and rods based on actual condition, wear, compatibility and the formation being encountered.
Attach the selected drill bits and rods, add rods as actual hole depth increases and change worn or unsuitable bits under the established physical operating procedure.
outputs: completed rod additions and bit changes

tasks.design: Retain the equipment instructions in {DOCS} and the driller's physical selection and fitting work. Lookup, selection and attachment have been considered separately; no record-writing or send is required by this task and no supported software change removes its labour.
tasks.previous_blocker: The work depends on actual component condition and physical attachment.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing instructions can support selection but do not perform fitting or judge actual wear.
tasks.still_hard: Changing formations, damaged components and safe handling require an experienced operator.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise unsuitable or worn equipment and complete the physical change correctly.
tasks.altitude: The work week and decision rights remain unchanged.

evidence.claim: Document lookup alone does not remove the physical labour of fitting drill components.

assumptions: Boundary is choosing and physically fitting bits and rods, not drilling the hole or producing a separate maintenance report. Shares are illustrative, not measured.

The driller obtains hole depth and actual formation from current work, observes component condition and reads equipment compatibility information in s1-s2. These are human observations and existing documents; no structured sensor feed or free data producer is assumed. Missing information requires manual inspection or clarification.
Native document lookup was considered and is assumed already available. No required record, report or send is hidden in the physical step; adding one would invent a baseline duty.
No software action commits a record, sends instructions or operates equipment. Existing physical work procedures remain unchanged. No new tool means zero incremental upkeep.
research_questions: Is there any demonstrated repeated lookup beyond the existing instruction access?

already_counted.description: Consult compatibility information and select components from actual condition.

incremental.description: No new tool or changed maintenance duty.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Existing lookup, selection and all physical fitting retain full time. No software or robotics mechanism is claimed to change the actual work.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Choose the drill for the ground and job

steps.what: Assess the actual job, access and known rock or soil conditions, including uncertainty in the ground information.
Read the available drills' operating envelopes and constraints in existing equipment instructions in {DOCS}.
Select the appropriate drill using knowledge of the rock or soil conditions, job requirements and equipment limits; resolve uncertain suitability before proceeding.

tasks.design: Retain the driller's site assessment and equipment choice, supported by the existing specifications in {DOCS}. Native lookup was considered separately from the judgement; no extra ordering, approval form or report is created to manufacture a saving.
tasks.previous_blocker: Unknown ground conditions and actual site constraints limit reliable drill selection.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing equipment specifications inform the choice but do not decide ground suitability.
tasks.still_hard: A nominal equipment rating may not capture the actual formation and access constraints.
tasks.human_edge: Choose equipment with a defensible margin for uncertain ground conditions.
tasks.altitude: The driller's judgement and work remain unchanged.

evidence.claim: Equipment specifications support drill selection but do not resolve uncertain actual ground conditions.

assumptions: Boundary is the equipment-selection decision. Moving, ordering and operating the drill are separate tasks. Shares are illustrative.

The driller verifies intended hole purpose, ground information, access constraints and equipment limits directly in s1-s2. Manual document review is already counted; no inferred ground classification or free sensor feed is assumed.
Native specification lookup is already available in this scenario. The task requires no separate record write or send; no administrative baseline is invented.
No system commits or sends a decision or operates machinery. Existing selection responsibility remains with the driller. No changed tool means zero incremental upkeep.
unknowns: Actual ground information and its uncertainty
research_questions: Is repeated specification navigation a material current burden beyond the existing lookup?

already_counted.description: Assess conditions, review equipment limits and choose the drill.

incremental.description: No new tool or changed upkeep.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Actual site assessment, existing specification lookup and equipment judgement all retain full time. No supported change removes any step.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Observe the material and geological changes actually encountered during drilling, relate them to depth and recognise uncertainty in recovered material.
Write the actual formation descriptions, depth intervals, sample references and observation uncertainty in the current field log.

Prepare the final formation log in borehole logging software {OTHER}; configure native depth-interval rows and log formatting to reuse entered values, then check all descriptions, intervals, sample references and uncertain boundaries against the source log.
Save the checked final geological formation log in the borehole logging software {OTHER}.

tasks.design: Configure native interval rows and log formatting in borehole logging software {OTHER}. The driller retains observation and first description capture, while native formatting reduces repeated construction of the final log and the driller checks it before save.
tasks.previous_blocker: Final formation logs repeatedly rebuilt depth rows and formatting from field entries.
tasks.enabler_now: Native borehole log configuration can format explicit interval and sample fields without classifying the formation.
tasks.still_hard: Mixed recovery, uncertain depth boundaries and changing geology need experienced observation.
tasks.human_edge: Describe what was encountered without overstating geological certainty.
tasks.altitude: Less final-log formatting; observation and source writing remain.

evidence.claim: Borehole logging tools can format explicit depth intervals and descriptions without determining the geology.

assumptions: Boundary is documenting formations through the stored geological log, not operating the drill or scientific interpretation by a geologist. Shares are an adoption scenario.

The driller produces job and hole IDs, actual interval start and end, depth unit, observed description, sample reference, observation time and uncertainty in s1-s2. Manual description entry and checking remain fully counted. Missing recovery is labelled, not filled with guessed geology.

Native log configuration is tried before code. Only repeated final row layout and formatting lose time; source writing and observation do not. No free automatic lithology recognition or new sensor capture is assumed.

s3's ordinary author check binds the completed final log for s4. Edits invalidate approval. The progress record in task 13680 references this existing log instead of duplicating the geological descriptions.
research_questions: Can native log formatting preserve uncertain interval boundaries and missing recovery?

already_counted.description: Check final formation log assembly against source descriptions and depths.

incremental.description: Maintain interval fields and validate final-log formatting.

approvals.approved_version: Final geological formation log checked at the end of s3

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Native formatting removes 50% of the 19-hour final-log preparation share: 9.5 gross hours less 2 upkeep. Zero if already configured or no separate final-log preparation exists. All observation, first capture and save time remain.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Record actual drilling progress with geological references

steps.what: Read actual drilling depth, completed work intervals, elapsed work and delays from the current drilling operation and its available indicators.
Capture the actual progress values, work periods and delays in the current drilling field record.
Read and verify the matching stored geological formation log by hole and depth interval so the progress record references the actual geology without rewriting the underlying observations.
Assemble the drilling progress and geological-data record in borehole logging software {OTHER}; configure native interval links and depth and time totals while preserving the source progress entries.
Check the final drilling progress record, actual depths and work periods, delay descriptions and geological references against both source records; resolve discrepancies before save.
Save the checked final drilling progress record in the borehole logging software {OTHER}.

tasks.design: Configure native progress rows, totals and geological-log references in borehole logging software {OTHER}. The driller captures actual work and checks the combined record; existing geological observations are linked as an input rather than counted twice.
tasks.previous_blocker: Progress totals and the matching geological references were repeatedly assembled from separate records.
tasks.enabler_now: Native interval links and simple depth and time formulas can reuse explicit source entries.
tasks.still_hard: Unclear work periods and inconsistent depth references require the driller's correction.
tasks.human_edge: Distinguish actual drilled progress from a planned depth or an uncertain reading.

ambition.what: No new billing or drilling-operation authority.

tasks.altitude: Less repeated progress assembly; physical drilling and source recording remain unchanged.

evidence.claim: Native logging records can link intervals and calculate explicit depth and time totals without inferring completed work.

assumptions: Boundary is the operational progress record with geological references. Formation observation and description belong to task 13686 and are existing inputs here, not duplicated labour or saving. Actual drilling and billing are separate. Shares are illustrative.

The driller captures job and hole IDs, actual start and end time, depth values and unit, work status and delay in s1-s2, then verifies formation-log revision and matching interval in s3. Manual observation, entry and mismatch resolution are counted. No rig telemetry is assumed; planned depth or scheduled time never establishes actual completion.
Try native logging configuration before code. Savings are repeated totals and record assembly only, not drilling time, initial capture, geological judgement or system runtime.
s5's ordinary final check binds the completed record saved in s6. Changes invalidate approval. The save has its full one-hour share and no external send is introduced.
unknowns: Compatibility of operational and formation depth references
research_questions: Can native interval links keep progress and formation revisions traceable without copying descriptions?

already_counted.description: Review native assembly and final progress-record consistency.

incremental.description: Maintain progress totals and geological-reference mappings.

approvals.approved_version: Final drilling progress record checked at the end of s5

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Native assembly removes 40% of the 25-hour progress assembly share: 10 gross hours less 2 upkeep. Zero if already configured. Actual progress observation, first capture, source matching, final check and save remain fully retained.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Earth drillers retain equipment selection and physical work; native logs reduce repeated formatting and progress totals only.
reach: Clarify equipment limits with construction equipment operators
Review progress references with first-line construction supervisors
role.ambitious_version: Maintain traceable actual drilling and geological records without substituting generated data for field observations.
